2609.30611.title: Epstein Files Engine: Agentic Search for Investigative Journalism
2609.30611.paper_summary: On Jan. 30, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice released a mixed-media collection concerning Jeffrey Epstein, including about three million pages of PDFs. We describe the Epstein Files Engine, an A.I. agent The New York Times deployed to investigate the files. The Engine translated reporter questions into Google BigQuery SQL queries across three corpora: Epstein-related releases, the Times's archive and external, Epstein-related news headlines. It used an LLM to plan queries and returned citation-rich answers a reporter could verify and trust. More than 100 journalists used the Engine, and it contributed to at least 20 published stories. We report how reporters queried it and describe Diff, our text-and-visual duplicate matching method that amplified novelty signals and allowed the Engine to surface genuinely new information. We argue that newsroom agents serve newsrooms best not as autonomous writers, but as interfaces to source material and institutional knowledge.
2609.30611.paper_summary_zh: 在2026年1月30日，美國司法部發布了一個關於傑弗瑞·愛潑斯坦的混合媒體資料集，包括約三百萬頁的PDF檔案。我們描述了愛潑斯坦檔案引擎，這是一個《紐約時報》部署的人工智慧代理，用於調查這些檔案。該引擎將記者的問題轉換為Google BigQuery SQL查詢，涵蓋三個語料庫：與愛潑斯坦相關的發布、時報的檔案以及外部的愛潑斯坦相關新聞標題。它使用了一個大型語言模型來規劃查詢，並返回了記者可以驗證和信任的豐富引用答案。超過100名記者使用了該引擎，並且它為至少20篇已發表的故事做出了貢獻。我們報告了記者如何查詢它，並描述了Diff，我們的文本和視覺重複匹配方法，這增強了新穎信號並使引擎能夠呈現真正的新資訊。我們認為，新聞室代理最適合的角色不是作為自主寫作的作者，而是作為來源材料和制度知識的介面。
